skill.name: dotnet-architect

content.value_statement: Complex .NET systems need clear architecture, reliable data access, and measurable performance. This skill guides production-ready C#, ASP.NET Core, testing, caching, and deployment decisions.
actual_capabilities: Designs ASP.NET Core APIs, microservices, middleware pipelines, dependency injection, authentication, and health checks.
Recommends EF Core and Dapper patterns for transactions, migrations, query performance, and connection management.
Reviews async code, LINQ usage, memory allocation, caching, and database access for performance risks.
Plans unit and integration testing with xUnit, mocking, WebApplicationFactory, containers, and coverage tools.
Applies clean architecture, domain-driven design, CQRS, observability, containerization, and deployment patterns.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not execute builds, tests, migrations, or deployments.
Requires application code, constraints, and workload details for recommendations tailored to a specific system.
A referenced implementation playbook is not included in the published skill package.
Security, performance, and deployment advice still requires validation in the target environment.

use_cases.title: Modernize an ASP.NET Core API
use_cases.description: Review an existing API and create a prioritized plan for structure, async behavior, data access, testing, security, and performance.

use_cases.title: Define Enterprise Service Boundaries
use_cases.description: Compare modular monolith, vertical slice, and microservice options using scale, ownership, consistency, and operational constraints.

use_cases.title: Prepare a .NET Service for Production
use_cases.description: Plan containers, health checks, telemetry, resilience, configuration, and deployment controls for a production service.

prompt_templates.title: Structure a New API
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain a suitable ASP.NET Core structure for [application]. Cover projects, dependency injection, configuration, validation, and testing.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Backend Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this C# or ASP.NET Core design: [details]. Identify correctness, async, security, maintainability, and performance issues. Prioritize recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Data Access Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design data access for [workload] using EF Core, Dapper, or both. Address transactions, query performance, migrations, testing, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Scalable Architecture Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an architecture proposal for [system] at [scale]. Include service boundaries, caching, resilience, observability, security, deployment, tradeoffs, and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Architect evaluating a complex production system

output_examples.input: Design caching for a product catalog with 100,000 items.
output: Use local memory for short-lived hot data and Redis as the shared cache.
Apply cache-aside reads, event-driven invalidation, randomized expiration, and explicit stale-data limits.
Measure hit rate, latency, eviction, and database fallback behavior before release.

output_examples.input: Review an asynchronous order handler for reliability and performance.
output: Pass cancellation tokens through every asynchronous dependency and avoid blocking calls.
Define transaction boundaries around durable state changes and make retries idempotent.
Add structured logs, latency metrics, integration tests, and failure-path tests.

output_examples.input: Choose between EF Core and Dapper for a reporting service.
output: Use EF Core for transactional workflows and maintainable domain persistence.
Use Dapper for measured reporting queries that need precise SQL and mapping control.
Keep transaction ownership explicit and benchmark representative workloads before adopting a mixed approach.

best_practices: Provide workload, latency, consistency, deployment, and team constraints before requesting an architecture.
Share relevant code and observed metrics when asking for performance or reliability reviews.
Request tradeoffs, validation steps, and test coverage with every recommended design.
anti_patterns: Do not request a complete architecture without business boundaries, scale, or operational constraints.
Do not apply microservices, repositories, CQRS, or caching without a demonstrated need.
Do not treat generated examples as production-ready before testing security, failure behavior, and performance.

faq.question: Which .NET areas does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers modern C#, ASP.NET Core, EF Core, Dapper, caching, testing, architecture patterns, observability, containers, and deployment.

faq.question: Can it review an existing codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the relevant code, architecture context, constraints, and observed problems for a focused review.

faq.question: Does it choose between EF Core and Dapper?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares maintainability, query control, transactions, performance evidence, and team experience for the stated workload.

faq.question: Can it produce deployment guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan Docker, Kubernetes, health checks, configuration, telemetry, logging, and continuous delivery practices.

faq.question: Does it run or validate generated code?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance, so users must build, test, profile, and review results in their own environment.

faq.question: What information improves the response?
faq.answer: Provide functional requirements, traffic, data volume, latency goals, consistency needs, infrastructure, team skills, and current code or diagrams.
